findings.issue_text: [BUG] The if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which the ERB handler compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` with no modifier condition — invalid Ruby syntax that fails at template compilation. Every render of the embed page raises ActionView::Template::Error (SyntaxError) and returns a 500, so after the 30-second reload triggered by loading.html.erb the iframe permanently shows an error instead of comments; the controller specs do not catch it because rspec controller specs do not render views.

[BUG] `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, a method added in Ruby 2.1.0 (released Dec 25, 2013, after this change); on the Ruby versions this repository runs (1.9.3/2.0.0 per its CI matrix and documented requirements) the method does not exist. The first execution with feed_polling_enabled raises NoMethodError (undefined method `scrub' for String), and because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false the hourly poll fails on every run and no feed item is ever imported; TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve's synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` path crashes identically, so embed retrieval also breaks whenever feed polling is enabled.

[BUG] embed.js and embed.css.scss are new top-level assets but nothing in the diff registers them in config.assets.precompile; Rails' default precompile list only covers application.js/application.css plus non-JS/CSS files, and the explicit extension Discourse maintains for admin.js et al. is not touched by this diff. In production (config.assets.compile = false) stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' in layouts/embed.html.erb raises AssetNotPrecompiledError so the embed page 500s, and /assets/embed.js — the URL external sites must script-tag to use the feature — returns 404; the embedding feature only works in development.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed#import_remote calls open(url) but never requires open-uri; the diff's only `require 'open-uri'` sits in Jobs::PollFeed, which is never loaded on the RetrieveTopic path when feed polling is disabled (the default). When open-uri is not loaded in the Sidekiq process, Kernel#open treats the URL as a filesystem path and the retrieval job fails with Errno::ENOENT, leaving the embedded iframe stuck on 'Loading Discussion...'; the code only works today if the ruby-readability gem happens to require open-uri internally, a transitive dependency the diff does not control.

[ADVISORY] The two new gems are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is regenerated; the repository's primary Gemfile.lock is left without ruby-readability and simple-rss, breaking the lockfiles-in-lockstep invariant this repo maintains during the Rails 3.2/4 transition. The default (Rails 3.2) bundle no longer matches the Gemfile: bundle exec in a fresh checkout fails to resolve the new gems until bundle install rewrites the lock, and the next contributor silently commits a regenerated Gemfile.lock mixed into unrelated work.

[ADVISORY] feed_key builds a 'feed-modified:<sha1>' Redis key that nothing in the diff ever reads or writes — the method has no caller anywhere in the new class. Maintainers reading the job assume a conditional-GET/Last-Modified caching mechanism exists, but every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the full feed; the dead method should either be deleted or wired into poll_feed.

[BUG] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds with no failure or terminal state, so any retrieval that never produces a topic leaves the embed in an endless reload loop. When retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username unset or misspelled, article host != embeddable_host, fetch/readability error), every viewer's iframe reloads forever, and each reload re-requests embed/best which enqueues another RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job (embed_controller.rb line 10) — unbounded job growth per viewer for permanently failing URLs.

[BUG] Feed content is imported with no sanitization: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) is passed straight into TopicEmbed.import → PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, whose cook path returns the raw string untouched, and it is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb and on topic pages. Any HTML in the feed executes on the forum origin — entity-escaped code samples that unescapeHTML turns into live tags break rendering, and script/iframe/onerror markup in a compromised or ad-laden feed becomes stored XSS.

[BUG] The item loop has no error handling and i.content is nil for feed items without a content element (RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide description), so CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError. With sidekiq_options retry: false the run aborts at the first bad item and every subsequent hourly run crashes at the same item, so items after it are never imported — the feed is permanently stuck with no recovery path.

[BUG] absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs: protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/x.png) match start_with?('/') and are rewritten to <forum>//cdn.example.com/x.png, while bare-relative URLs (page.html) are left untouched and resolve against the forum's URL. Images and links in imported articles that use protocol-relative or bare-relative URLs (common in real feeds) point at the wrong host or 404, breaking every imported post containing them.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff covers Jobs::RetrieveTopic — the diff adds specs for TopicRetriever, EmbedController, PollFeed's gates and TopicEmbed, but no spec/jobs/retrieve_topic_spec.rb. The job's InvalidParameters guard and the `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` staff-bypass decision are unverified; a regression there silently throttles staff-triggered retrievals or removes the throttle for anonymous ones.

[ADVISORY] The only positive test stubs poll_feed itself (`poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`), so the parsing loop — nil content handling, the i.id URL fallback, the user lookup — has zero coverage. A regression in poll_feed's body (e.g., the nil-content NoMethodError) ships undetected because no spec ever executes it.

[ADVISORY] No test renders the new templates: the controller spec lacks render_views, so best.html.erb, loading.html.erb and layouts/embed.html.erb are never compiled or executed by any spec in the diff. Template-level failures (nil post.user in best.html.erb, blank logo_url, ERB errors) ship undetected and surface only as 500s inside production iframes.

[BUG] The Disqus import now performs a live HTTP fetch per thread via TopicEmbed.import_remote with no error handling, where the previous implementation created posts locally with no network dependency. One dead, redirecting or slow link raises OpenURI::HTTPError and aborts the entire import mid-run, leaving a partial import with no resume path.

[BUG] Nothing cleans up topic_embeds when its topic is deleted, and best never re-enqueues retrieval once topic_id_for_embed returns an id, so a deleted imported topic leaves an orphaned row. The embed for that URL renders the forum's error page forever and never re-imports the article, with no recovery short of manual DB surgery.

[ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic SETNX followed by EXPIRE; a crash between the two calls leaves the retrieved:<url> key with no TTL. That embed URL is then silently throttled forever (retrieve no-ops on every request) until someone manually deletes the Redis key.

[BUG] topic_embeds.embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index, but import performs no length check before TopicEmbed.create!. Importing an article whose URL exceeds 255 characters (routine with tracking query strings) raises 'data too long' and crashes the import — or on non-strict MySQL silently truncates the URL, breaking subsequent lookups and colliding on the unique index.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is dead code — defined but never called anywhere in the diff — leftover from an unimplemented conditional-GET/If-Modified-Since check. It misleads readers into thinking changed-feed detection exists, while the job actually re-fetches and re-parses the entire feed every hour, relying solely on content_sha1 dedupe; deleting the method removes the false implication.

[BUG] embed.js throws TypeError (appendChild on null) when the publisher's page has no element with id 'discourse-comments', and the throw also prevents the resize postMessage listener from ever being attached. A publisher who misconfigures the snippet gets a silent console error and no comments, with no diagnostic pointing at the missing container.

[BUG] The raw_html cook path added for imports returns post.raw verbatim, bypassing the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline, and nothing in this diff sanitizes the imported content it feeds into that path (poll_feed.rb:35 stores raw feed HTML; embed/best.html.erb:23 renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`). Untrusted third-party HTML is persisted as the post body and rendered as-is on the Discourse origin: any event-handler markup or script in a polled RSS item (or a javascript: href surviving readability's tag whitelist on the import_remote path, which whitelists a[href] with no scheme check) executes in the embed iframe and on normal topic pages — stored XSS. The 'validation system' named in the intent covers only host/URL checks; content validation is entirely absent.

[BUG] The unrelated CreateTopTopics migration is modified to add `force: true` to create_table — work with no traceable connection to the embedding feature. create_table with force: true drops the existing table, so any manual re-run of this already-shipped migration (db:migrate:redo, replaying migrations against a restored DB) silently destroys all materialized top_topics ranking data; the change also smuggles an unrelated destructive edit into this PR.

[BUG] The existing Disqus import tool is rewritten to route through TopicEmbed.import_remote and its `--category` option is deleted outright — behavior changes to an existing user-facing tool not traceable to any embedding requirement in this diff. Existing automation invoking `thor disqus:import -c 'Category'` loses category assignment with no replacement, and imports now fetch each thread's link over HTTP and import the remote article body instead of building topics from the local Disqus XML — threads whose link is dead or non-http make import return nil so the thread and all its posts are silently skipped.

[BUG] URL validation is split across two components with different semantics: EmbedController#best (embed_controller.rb:15) accepts any embed_url as long as the referer host matches embeddable_host, while TopicRetriever#invalid_host? silently drops any embed_url whose own host differs from embeddable_host. An embeddable page pointing the iframe at an article on a different host renders the loading page and re-enqueues a retrieve_topic job on every 30-second reload forever — the job no-ops on the host check before the throttle is even set, so the visitor sees 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely with no error signal and the job queue absorbs repeated no-op work per viewer.

[ADVISORY] PollFeed#feed_key builds a 'feed-modified:<sha1>' redis key that no code in this diff ever reads or writes. Dead code implying conditional/304-style polling that was never implemented; the next maintainer tuning the poller will assume Last-Modified tracking exists and skip adding it, leaving the hourly job re-parsing and re-hashing the full feed indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] The spec only exercises the three execute() gating conditions and the delegation to poll_feed; none of the new parsing logic in poll_feed (item iteration, the i.id URL fallback at poll_feed.rb:32-33, content scrubbing, the TopicEmbed.import call) is touched by any test in this diff. A regression in the URL fallback or content handling ships green — feed imports would silently create topics keyed to the wrong URLs or crash the hourly job, with no test failing to catch it.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed assumes every feed item has content and a usable title: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when i.content is nil (description-only RSS feeds carry no content:encoded), and a nil i.title flows straight into PostCreator under skip_validations. One content-less item aborts the entire poll run, and because the job is declared with `sidekiq_options retry: false` it stays broken until the next hourly attempt hits the same item again; title-less items produce nil-titled topics.

[ADVISORY] Whitespace-only edits (trailing-space removal on line 4 and removal of the file's final newline) to the unrelated MigrateWordCounts migration. Untraceable churn in a shipped migration pollutes git blame on db/migrate files and invites merge conflicts for zero functional change; the stripped trailing newline is also a regression in file hygiene.

[BUG] The if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which ERB/Erubis compiles to `...; end if; _erbout << ...` — `end if` with no condition expression is a Ruby SyntaxError raised the first time the template is compiled. Every GET /embed/best that reaches rendering raises a template SyntaxError and returns 500, so the entire embed feature is dead on arrival; the new controller spec does not enable render_views, so CI stays green while production is red (a stand-in guard).

[BUG] poll_feed calls `i.content.scrub` on every feed item, but simple-rss only populates `content` for feeds carrying content:encoded/atom:content, so on a standard RSS 2.0 feed (description-only) `i.content` is nil and the first item raises NoMethodError. With `sidekiq_options retry: false` the run aborts at the first content-less item: items after it are never imported, and every hourly run crashes at the same item, so RSS import permanently stalls for the most common feed format.

[BUG] Article identity is the raw embed_url string with no canonicalization: the on-demand path stores the client-supplied discourseEmbedUrl (topic_id_for_embed at lines 78-79 does an exact-string match) while PollFeed stores the feed item's link, so the same article gets two rows when the two strings differ in any cosmetic way (fragment, query order, trailing slash, http/https). TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve polls the feed, then falls back to fetch_http when its exact-string `exists?` check misses (lib/topic_retriever.rb:42), so an article whose page URL differs textually from its feed link is deterministically imported twice as two separate topics; the unique index enforces string uniqueness, not article identity.

[BUG] No code path in the diff removes the TopicEmbed row when its topic or post is deleted (no destroy hook, and Topic/Post are not modified to cascade), leaving a dangling topic_id/post_id with no invalidation. After an admin deletes an imported topic, topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic_id so the embed page renders a 404/broken view forever, and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve's `exists?` check treats the orphaned row as already-retrieved, permanently blocking re-import of that URL until someone deletes the row manually.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously runs the entire feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) inside the per-URL RetrieveTopic job, duplicating the scheduler's responsibility on a user-triggered path. Every embed of a not-yet-imported article re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed inline (open + parse + one topic per item), so the requesting user's article appears only after the full poll finishes, and N users embedding different articles concurrently run N overlapping full polls that race on the same feed items.

[ADVISORY] import is check-then-insert (`where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`) with no rescue of ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique; the unique index closes the data-integrity hole but turns the race into a raised exception. When two paths import the same URL concurrently (two users embedding the same fresh article, or PollFeed racing RetrieveTopic), the loser's create! raises inside the job — for PollFeed (retry: false) that aborts the run and skips every remaining feed item for that hour.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus import was rewired onto TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently dropping the `--category` option (removed from method_option), the `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` pass-through, and its previous zero-network-dependency behavior. Scripted imports that pass `-c` break; imported topics lose their original Disqus dates (created_at becomes import time); and each thread now requires a live HTTP fetch with no error handling, so one dead/404 link aborts the whole bulk import mid-run with no resume or report.

[ADVISORY] The loading view reloads every 30 seconds with no terminal failure state, while every reload of /embed/best re-enqueues a RetrieveTopic job (embed_controller.rb:15). When retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username unset or misspelled, remote fetch error, misconfigured feed URL), every viewer polls the forum and re-enqueues a job every 30 seconds indefinitely, with no error surfaced to the admin, the embedding site, or the reader.

[ADVISORY] The spec only asserts the three SiteSetting guards and a delegation stub; the item loop in PollFeed#poll_feed — feed parsing, the link/id fallback, i.content handling, and the import call — has zero coverage in this diff. The feature's real logic (where the nil-content crash at poll_feed.rb:35 lives) ships green; any regression in feed parsing or import silently breaks RSS import with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined but never called anywhere in the diff — the conditional-GET (If-Modified-Since) check it was built for was never wired into poll_feed. Every hourly poll re-fetches and re-parses the full feed and re-hashes every item even when nothing changed, and the dead method misleads maintainers into believing modified-checking exists; deleting it loses nothing.

[ADVISORY] The migration hardcodes `default: 1`, duplicating Post.cook_methods' positional mapping (:regular = 1) instead of deriving it, so the meaning of every stored cook_method value is coupled to member order in the Enum. The next editor who inserts a cook method before :raw_html (or reorders members) silently redefines the meaning of every existing row in the posts table with no error anywhere; nothing cross-checks the migration constant against the Enum.

[ADVISORY] The update path revises only the post body — `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` passes no title — so the topic title is written once at creation and never again. When a source article's headline changes (routine for news/editorial feeds), the content updates but the topic keeps the stale title forever, and the schema/model offers no way to express a title update.

[ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? uses `$redis.setnx` followed by `$redis.expire` as two separate non-atomic calls instead of a single SET with expiry. If the process dies or the expire call fails between the two calls, the key persists with no TTL and that embed_url is throttled forever — retrieved_recently? returns true on every subsequent attempt, so the article can never be imported until someone manually deletes the Redis key.

[ADVISORY] `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255), but article URLs routinely exceed 255 characters with tracking query strings, and the column backs a unique index. A long URL makes TopicEmbed.create! raise ('value too long' on PostgreSQL, error on strict MySQL) and crash the importing job, or silently truncate on non-strict MySQL so two distinct long URLs collide on the unique index and import the wrong article's match.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores third-party HTML (RSS item content passed through CGI.unescapeHTML, or article HTML fetched from the embed URL) as post content with cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw string and skips the sanitizing rendering pipeline entirely; embed/best.html.erb then renders post.cooked with `raw`. A malicious or compromised feed or article yields stored JavaScript execution on the Discourse origin — in the embed iframe and on regular topic pages that render cooked — enabling session theft and moderator actions on behalf of visitors. CGI.unescapeHTML actively converts entity-encoded markup back into live tags, and the footer interpolates the unescaped #{url} into an HTML attribute, so even a well-behaved feed's link field is an injection vector. The new spec cements the invariant drop by asserting post.cooked == post.raw.

[BUG] The header if/else is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end` followed by a condition-less `if` that then swallows the following statements and leaves the block tree unbalanced), so the template raises a SyntaxError when compiled. Every /embed/best request that finds a topic_id fails at template compile time and returns 500 instead of the embedded discussion — once the background retrieval succeeds, the comments never render for anyone; the success-path controller specs in this same diff fail on this too.

[BUG] `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls String#scrub, which does not exist on the Ruby this app runs (the Gemfile states the project targets 1.9; String#scrub shipped in Ruby 2.1), so poll_feed raises NoMethodError on every execution. With feed_polling_enabled, the hourly job crashes before importing anything, so feed-based embedding never imports a single item. Additionally the loop has no per-item rescue, so even on a Ruby with scrub, one item with nil content (plain RSS 2.0 description-only feeds) or nil title aborts all remaining items for that run, every run.

[BUG] The success-path example stubs TopicView.new with only an expectation and no .returns, so @topic_view is nil, rendering best.html.erb raises NoMethodError on @topic_view.posts, and the after-hook's response.should be_success assertion fails. The spec suite fails on this diff, and the only test covering the found-topic render path never actually exercised it — the happy path of the embed feature shipped unverified.

[BUG] The --category option and the category_id lookup/assignment logic are removed from disqus:import with no replacement, an objective change to a public task bundled into a PR about embed URL handling. Existing automation invoking `thor disqus:import -c SomeCategory` now aborts with Thor's unknown-option error before importing anything, and imported threads can no longer be placed into a category; nothing in the diff migrates or documents the removed capability.

[ADVISORY] disqus:import now fetches each thread's link over the network via TopicEmbed.import_remote (open(url).read) instead of building the topic entirely from the export file. Any dead link, timeout, or non-HTML response raises inside the threads loop and aborts the remaining import mid-run, where the previous implementation created the permalink topic locally with no HTTP dependency — a large historical import now fails wholesale on the first unreachable URL.

[ADVISORY] The update path assumes embed.post is present, but nothing cleans up the topic_embeds row when an imported topic is deleted (no dependent: destroy, no FK), so embed.post becomes nil. After an admin deletes an imported topic, the next content change makes PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raise NoMethodError, crashing the hourly PollFeed run and skipping all remaining feed items, while topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the deleted topic's id so the embed iframe renders a dead topic forever.

[ADVISORY] The PollFeed spec only asserts the three gating settings and that execute delegates to poll_feed; the parsing/import loop itself (link fallback to i.id, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import per item) has zero test coverage. The per-item crash behavior and URL/title handling ship completely untested — which is exactly where the NoMethodError defects in poll_feed live — so any regression in the actual import logic passes CI silently.

[ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? uses SETNX followed by a separate EXPIRE, so a worker killed between the two calls leaves the throttle key in Redis with no TTL. After such a crash (e.g., a deploy restarting Sidekiq mid-job), that embed URL is permanently throttled — TopicRetriever never fetches it again and visitors see 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely until someone manually deletes the key from Redis.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs as site-relative because they start with '/', rewriting src='//cdn.example.com/x' to 'http://blog.example.com//cdn.example.com/x'. Images and links from feeds or articles that use scheme-relative URLs (common for CDN-hosted assets) render broken inside imported posts, with no error surfaced to the admin configuring the feed.

[ADVISORY] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds with no terminal failure state, and each reload of /embed/best re-enqueues a retrieve_topic job (throttled only to once per 60 seconds per URL). When retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username blank or misconfigured, article unfetchable), every visitor's iframe loops on 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely while the job queue absorbs a retrieve job per embedded URL per minute, and nothing surfaces the misconfiguration to the admin.

[BUG] RSS item content is passed through CGI.unescapeHTML and imported with zero HTML sanitization as a post with cook_method raw_html, so feed-supplied markup including <script> tags and inline event handlers is stored verbatim and rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:17 (and on normal topic pages, since Post#cook returns raw unmodified for raw_html). Anyone who can influence the polled feed's content (reader comments embedded in the feed, a compromised or third-party feed the admin points at) gets stored XSS on the forum origin: script executes for every viewer of the embedded comments or the imported topic, enabling session/cookie theft of admins; no sanitizer runs anywhere on this path.

[BUG] The source URL is interpolated unescaped into the imported post's HTML footer (`#{url}`), so a URL containing a single quote — which Ruby's URI parser accepts in query strings, e.g. `http://host/?y='onmouseover='alert(1)` — breaks out of the single-quoted href attribute, and feed-supplied links (PollFeed passes i.link through with only a ^http prefix regex) can inject arbitrary tags including

[BUG] The SSRF guard compares only the initial URL's host string against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but the actual fetch in TopicEmbed.import_remote (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48) uses open(), which follows cross-host http->http redirects, and a string host comparison is defeated by DNS rebinding, so the fetch is not actually confined to the embeddable host. A malicious or compromised embedding site — the exact third party this feature admits — returns a 302 to an internal address (cloud metadata, internal services); open-uri follows it and the response body is imported as a public post, giving internal-network SSRF with read/exfiltration through the public topic, triggerable by any anonymous visitor with a spoofed Referer.

[BUG] The controller enqueues a retrieve_topic Sidekiq job for any user-supplied embed_url before any host validation or throttling runs (validation happens later inside the job via TopicRetriever), and TopicRetriever's throttle key is the full embed_url string, so varying the query string bypasses it entirely. Unauthenticated attackers (the Referer gate is satisfied by a spoofed header) flood the Sidekiq queue with arbitrary-length job payloads, create unbounded Redis keys via the per-URL setnx throttle, and trigger unbounded outbound fetches — a cheap queue/Redis exhaustion and fetch-amplification DoS against the forum.

[BUG] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) routes through Kernel#open, which only delegates strings matching the scheme pattern to OpenURI and falls back to the original Kernel#open for everything else, so a settings value beginning with `|` is executed as a shell command. A feed_polling_url of `|<command>` (config-backed sink; treat the settings store as attacker-influenceable input) executes arbitrary commands on the app server during the hourly poll — remote code execution, not merely SSRF.

[ADVISORY] The embeddability gate authenticates the client using the Referer header, which is fully client-controlled and trivially spoofed by any non-browser client. Every protection downstream of this check (triggering server-side fetches, enqueueing jobs, rendering the embed view) is available to any anonymous internet attacker with curl -H 'Referer: ...'; the control only stops naive browser embedding, so it must not be relied on as a security boundary for the retrieval pipeline it guards.

[ADVISORY] The ruby-readability allowlist preserves href values without any scheme validation, so javascript: URLs present in the source article survive extraction and are rendered raw in the embed page and topic. A reader clicking such a link in the embedded comments or the imported topic executes script in the forum origin — stored XSS via the same import path that the tag/attribute allowlist only partially mitigates; bites every viewer of imported articles from any source the admin imports from.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of origin equality, so any sender whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted. A page at an origin contained within discourseUrl (e.g. intranet host https://forum when discourseUrl is https://forum.example.com/) passes the check and can forge resize messages; impact is limited to iframe height manipulation on the embedding page, but the origin control is defective as written.

[BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never reaches params.require(:embed_url): the ensure_embeddable before_filter raises Discourse::InvalidAccess first (default-blank embeddable_host, and nil referer would also fail), so the test passes regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists. The missing-embed_url validation path (embed_controller.rb line 10) has zero coverage; replacing params.require(:embed_url) with params[:embed_url] lets nil flow into TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and Jobs.enqueue in production while this test and every other test in the diff stays green.

[BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, so execute short-circuits on the default-false feed_polling_enabled? and poll_feed is skipped before the clauses these tests claim to verify are ever evaluated. Both tests pass even if the feed_polling_url.present? or embed_by_username.present? clauses are deleted from Jobs::PollFeed#execute, giving false confidence that each setting independently gates the hourly job.

[ADVISORY] The only positive test verifies delegation by mocking poll_feed, so the entire poll_feed body — SimpleRSS parsing, the i.link/i.id URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and the TopicEmbed.import call — is never executed by any test (checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the only spec in the diff referencing PollFeed; every test interacts with poll_feed solely via mocha expectations). A regression in feed handling (e.g., i.content raising NoMethodError on feeds without a content element, or the URL fallback picking i.id) ships undetected; with sidekiq_options retry: false the hourly job then dies and imports silently stop in production.

[ADVISORY] Both positive-path tests stub retrieved_recently? and mock perform_retrieve, so the real throttle logic ($redis.setnx with 60-second expire), the TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists? dedupe, the feed-polling branch, and fetch_http's embed_by_username lookup are never executed (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb — the only spec referencing TopicRetriever; all five tests stub or mock these methods). A regression in the redis throttle (e.g., the key never expiring, permanently blocking retrieval for a URL) or in the dedupe/fetch internals passes the suite; the staff no_throttle bypass consumed here is likewise never exercised anywhere in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The update test only exercises the changed-content path: the unchanged-content dedup branch (content_sha1 equality short-circuit) is never executed and the persisted update of embed.content_sha1 via update_column is never asserted. A regression that drops embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) or breaks the sha1 comparison passes the suite while every hourly PollFeed run re-revises the same post, spamming post revisions indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] topic_embed_spec.rb covers only .import; TopicEmbed.import_remote — the Readability extraction with its tag/attribute whitelist and the opts[:title] || doc.title fallback that both TopicRetriever.fetch_http and the rewritten disqus:import task now depend on — is never called by any test, and .topic_id_for_embed is only ever mocked (embed_controller_spec.rb lines 41/49), never run against real data. A regression in import_remote (e.g., readability returning empty/nil content or the whitelist stripping everything) breaks on-demand embedding and the disqus import task while the suite stays green; a regression in topic_id_for_embed's query makes every embed request take the retrieve path.

[BUG] The header block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` with no condition expression after the `if` keyword, so the template fails ERB/Erubis compilation with a SyntaxError. [BUG] When no topic exists the controller fire-and-forgets Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) and renders a loading page whose only mechanism is an unconditional 30-second reload loop with no terminal state. [BUG] The 'retrieved recently' redis marker is committed (setnx + expire) before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed retrieval leaves the marker in place for its full 60-second TTL. Every retry within the next 60 seconds — retries of the failed job and the loading page's 30-second re-enqueues — enters retrieve, sees the marker, and returns success without attempting the work, so the system reports success while the retrieval never happened; recovery depends entirely on the user keeping the page open past the throttle window.

[BUG] setnx and expire are two separate redis calls, so a crash or redis error between them leaves the throttle key set with no TTL. The orphaned key makes retrieved_recently? return true forever for that embed_url, permanently and silently blocking retrieval for it (loading page forever) until someone manually deletes the key or Redis is flushed.

[BUG] perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline and lets its exceptions propagate, so embed retrieval is coupled to feed health and aborts before fetch_http is reached. With feed_polling_enabled and a broken feed (unreachable URL, non-feed response, or the per-item crash in the loop), every embed retrieval for every URL fails as a job error instead of falling through to the HTTP path; even a healthy feed forces each retrieval to run the entire feed import synchronously inside the job.

[BUG] import_remote buffers the entire response of open(url).read into memory with no size cap and passes no open/read timeout options. The fetch is reachable from the public embed flow for any URL whose host matches embeddable_host, so a large response exhausts the Sidekiq worker's memory, and a server that drips bytes slower than the per-read timeout keeps the worker hung indefinitely.

[BUG] The throttle key is the full embed_url string ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}"), so it imposes no limit across URLs, and EmbedController#best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job on every cache-miss request with no other rate limit. A client (the referer check is a client-supplied header) that varies the path on embeddable_host bypasses the throttle entirely, driving unbounded server-side fetch+import jobs and unbounded topic creation from a public endpoint.

[BUG] fetch_http returns silently when the embed_by_username setting does not resolve to an existing user (blank setting, typo, renamed account). Retrieval no-ops with no log line and no error result, so every embed on the site shows the loading page forever with nothing in the logs to explain why.

[ADVISORY] The dedup key is the embed_url string compared verbatim (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) and topic_id_for_embed) with no URL normalization anywhere in the import/lookup path. The same article reached via textually different URLs (trailing slash, http vs https, feed link vs the blog's canonical permalink) creates duplicate topics, and the embed iframe on one variant never finds the other variant's topic and re-triggers retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which the ERB handler compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` with no modifier condition — invalid Ruby syntax that fails at template compilation. Every render of the embed page raises ActionView::Template::Error (SyntaxError) and returns a 500, so after the 30-second reload triggered by loading.html.erb the iframe permanently shows an error instead of comments; the controller specs do not catch it because rspec controller specs do not render views.

[BUG] `i.content.scrub` calls String#scrub, a method added in Ruby 2.1.0 (released Dec 25, 2013, after this change); on the Ruby versions this repository runs (1.9.3/2.0.0 per its CI matrix and documented requirements) the method does not exist. The first execution with feed_polling_enabled raises NoMethodError (undefined method `scrub' for String), and because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false the hourly poll fails on every run and no feed item is ever imported; TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve's synchronous `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` path crashes identically, so embed retrieval also breaks whenever feed polling is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). If `i.content` is a String and the runtime Ruby lacks `String#scrub`, this will raise NoMethodError and abort the job; this is amplified by `sidekiq_options retry: false` in the same class, and TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when feed polling is enabled (lib/topic_retriever.rb), so the failure would repeatedly prevent imports/retrieval. The only non-verifiable part from the diff is the repository’s actual Ruby version support, so impact depends on whether Ruby < 2.1 is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] embed.js and embed.css.scss are new top-level assets but nothing in the diff registers them in config.assets.precompile; Rails' default precompile list only covers application.js/application.css plus non-JS/CSS files, and the explicit extension Discourse maintains for admin.js et al. is not touched by this diff. In production (config.assets.compile = false) stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' in layouts/embed.html.erb raises AssetNotPrecompiledError so the embed page 500s, and /assets/embed.js — the URL external sites must script-tag to use the feature — returns 404; the embedding feature only works in development.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds standalone assets `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and directly references the stylesheet via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`. The diff does not show these assets being pulled into an existing manifest (e.g., application.js/css) nor any update to an assets precompile list/config. In a typical Rails production setup where only explicitly-precompiled JS/CSS are built, this would lead to `embed.css`/`embed.js` not being available (AssetNotPrecompiledError / 404), breaking the new embedding feature outside development.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed#import_remote calls open(url) but never requires open-uri; the diff's only `require 'open-uri'` sits in Jobs::PollFeed, which is never loaded on the RetrieveTopic path when feed polling is disabled (the default). When open-uri is not loaded in the Sidekiq process, Kernel#open treats the URL as a filesystem path and the retrieval job fails with Errno::ENOENT, leaving the embedded iframe stuck on 'Loading Discussion...'; the code only works today if the ruby-readability gem happens to require open-uri internally, a transitive dependency the diff does not control.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicEmbed#import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) but does not `require 'open-uri'` anywhere in that file or in the retrieve path (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). The only added explicit `require 'open-uri'` is in `Jobs::PollFeed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), which is not guaranteed to be loaded/executed when feed polling is disabled (the default per site_settings.yml). Without open-uri loaded, `Kernel#open` won’t handle http(s) URLs and can raise errors, breaking embed retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two new gems are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is regenerated; the repository's primary Gemfile.lock is left without ruby-readability and simple-rss, breaking the lockfiles-in-lockstep invariant this repo maintains during the Rails 3.2/4 transition. The default (Rails 3.2) bundle no longer matches the Gemfile: bundle exec in a fresh checkout fails to resolve the new gems until bundle install rewrites the lock, and the next contributor silently commits a regenerated Gemfile.lock mixed into unrelated work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile`, and updates only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` to include them. There is no corresponding update to the (presumed) default lockfile (`Gemfile.lock`) in this diff. With Bundler, changing `Gemfile` without updating the lock typically causes `bundle exec`/`bundle check` in a fresh checkout to fail until `bundle install` regenerates the lock, so this is a real breakage if the repo expects lockfiles to stay in sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key builds a 'feed-modified:<sha1>' Redis key that nothing in the diff ever reads or writes — the method has no caller anywhere in the new class. Maintainers reading the job assume a conditional-GET/Last-Modified caching mechanism exists, but every hourly run re-downloads and re-parses the full feed; the dead method should either be deleted or wired into poll_feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `Jobs::PollFeed` defines `def feed_key` building a Redis key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`), but nothing in the diff calls `feed_key`, and `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without any conditional/cached fetch logic. This is dead/misleading code rather than a functional defect: the job still runs, but the unused method suggests a caching mechanism that isn’t implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds with no failure or terminal state, so any retrieval that never produces a topic leaves the embed in an endless reload loop. When retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username unset or misspelled, article host != embeddable_host, fetch/readability error), every viewer's iframe reloads forever, and each reload re-requests embed/best which enqueues another RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job (embed_controller.rb line 10) — unbounded job growth per viewer for permanently failing URLs.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally `document.location.reload()` every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) with no terminal/failure state. If retrieval never results in a `TopicEmbed` record (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is missing/blank, or remote fetch/readability fails), the iframe will reload forever and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job. While `TopicRetriever` throttles *work* via Redis (`retrieved_recently?`), it does not prevent repeated job enqueues, so job volume can grow with viewers for permanently failing URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Feed content is imported with no sanitization: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) is passed straight into TopicEmbed.import → PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, whose cook path returns the raw string untouched, and it is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb and on topic pages. Any HTML in the feed executes on the forum origin — entity-escaped code samples that unescapeHTML turns into live tags break rendering, and script/iframe/onerror markup in a compromised or ad-laden feed becomes stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds feed import via `Jobs::PollFeed`, which does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skip_validations: true)`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Nothing in the diff sanitizes the feed HTML, so arbitrary/compromised feed markup (e.g., `<script>`, event handlers, iframes) can become stored XSS on the forum origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The item loop has no error handling and i.content is nil for feed items without a content element (RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide description), so CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError. With sidekiq_options retry: false the run aborts at the first bad item and every subsequent hourly run crashes at the same item, so items after it are never imported — the feed is permanently stuck with no recovery path.

[BUG] absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs: protocol-relative URLs (//cdn.example.com/x.png) match start_with?('/') and are rewritten to <forum>//cdn.example.com/x.png, while bare-relative URLs (page.html) are left untouched and resolve against the forum's URL. Images and links in imported articles that use protocol-relative or bare-relative URLs (common in real feeds) point at the wrong host or 404, breaking every imported post containing them.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are rewritten only when `href/src.start_with?('/')` (root-relative). This mistakenly also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`: `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/x.png`, and the code rewrites it to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x.png` (wrong host/path). Bare-relative URLs like `page.html` are not rewritten at all, so in the imported `raw_html` post they will resolve relative to the Discourse page/host, likely breaking links/images. This behavior is directly implied by the diff and would break real-world feeds using these URL forms.

A regression in poll_feed's body (e.g., the nil-content NoMethodError) ships undetected because no spec ever executes it.

No spec actually calls `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, so none of its new logic is exercised: the `User.where(...).first` lookup/early return, RSS parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`), the per-item URL fallback to `i.id`, or the `i.content.scrub` call (which could raise if `i.content` is nil). Template-level failures (nil post.user in best.html.erb, blank logo_url, ERB errors) ship undetected and surface only as 500s inside production iframes.

In typical Rails controller specs, views/layouts are not rendered/compiled unless `render_views` is set, and there are no view specs for app/views/embed/best.html.erb, app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, or app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Disqus import now performs a live HTTP fetch per thread via TopicEmbed.import_remote with no error handling, where the previous implementation created posts locally with no network dependency. One dead, redirecting or slow link raises OpenURI::HTTPError and aborts the entire import mid-run, leaving a partial import with no resume path.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path was changed from creating a local post via `PostCreator` to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (and uses `Readability::Document`) without any `rescue`/error handling, so an `OpenURI::HTTPError`, timeout, redirect issue, etc. will raise and bubble up, aborting the Thor task mid-loop and leaving a partial import. This new network dependency + uncaught exceptions is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Nothing cleans up topic_embeds when its topic is deleted, and best never re-enqueues retrieval once topic_id_for_embed returns an id, so a deleted imported topic leaves an orphaned row. The embed for that URL renders the forum's error page forever and never re-imports the article, with no recovery short of manual DB surgery.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code branches solely on whether `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a value. If a `topic_embeds` row exists but the referenced topic has been deleted, `topic_id_for_embed` will still return the old `topic_id` (it just `pluck`s), so the controller will attempt `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` and will never enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` because the `else` only runs when `topic_id` is nil. This makes the embed unable to recover/re-import for that URL once the topic is gone unless the `topic_embeds` row is removed elsewhere (no such cleanup is shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? uses non-atomic SETNX followed by EXPIRE; a crash between the two calls leaves the retrieved:<url> key with no TTL. That embed URL is then silently throttled forever (retrieve no-ops on every request) until someone manually deletes the Redis key.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? throttling does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. Because these are separate Redis commands, a crash/process kill between them can leave `retrieved:<embed_url>` set without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see setnx fail and return true (throttled) forever until the key is manually deleted, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topic_embeds.embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index, but import performs no length check before TopicEmbed.create!. Importing an article whose URL exceeds 255 characters (routine with tracking query strings) raises 'data too long' and crashes the import — or on non-strict MySQL silently truncates the URL, breaking subsequent lookups and colliding on the unique index.

[BUG] `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls String#scrub, which does not exist on the Ruby this app runs (the Gemfile states the project targets 1.9; String#scrub shipped in Ruby 2.1), so poll_feed raises NoMethodError on every execution. With feed_polling_enabled, the hourly job crashes before importing anything, so feed-based embedding never imports a single item. Additionally the loop has no per-item rescue, so even on a Ruby with scrub, one item with nil content (plain RSS 2.0 description-only feeds) or nil title aborts all remaining items for that run, every run.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the new code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` (common for RSS feeds that only provide `description`), this will raise `NoMethodError` (`nil.scrub`) and abort the run. Also, `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies (e.g., 1.9/2.0), and the diff’s Gemfile comments indicate the app may target Ruby 1.9, in which case this line would crash every execution when feed polling is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The success-path example stubs TopicView.new with only an expectation and no .returns, so @topic_view is nil, rendering best.html.erb raises NoMethodError on @topic_view.posts, and the after-hook's response.should be_success assertion fails. adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not chain `.returns(...)`, so Mocha will make `TopicView.new` return `nil` by default. That means the controller assigns `@topic_view = nil` in the topic-found path. However, in typical RSpec controller specs views are not rendered (unless `render_views` is enabled), so this does not necessarily cause a failing `NoMethodError` on `@topic_view.posts` as the finding claims. The real, verifiable issue is that the “happy path” test is not validating that `@topic_view` is a usable `TopicView` instance (or that the template can render), because the mocked return value is wrong/missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The --category option and the category_id lookup/assignment logic are removed from disqus:import with no replacement, an objective change to a public task bundled into a PR about embed URL handling. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] disqus:import now fetches each thread's link over the network via TopicEmbed.import_remote (open(url).read) instead of building the topic entirely from the export file. Any dead link, timeout, or non-HTML response raises inside the threads loop and aborts the remaining import mid-run, where the previous implementation created the permalink topic locally with no HTTP dependency — a large historical import now fails wholesale on the first unreachable URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `disqus:import` to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), which does `open(url).read` with no error handling (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Network errors (dead link, timeout, non-HTML, etc.) will raise inside the threads loop and abort the import run, whereas the previous implementation created the initial topic locally from the export data without any HTTP dependency. This is a concrete new failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update path assumes embed.post is present, but nothing cleans up the topic_embeds row when an imported topic is deleted (no dependent: destroy, no FK), so embed.post becomes nil. After an admin deletes an imported topic, the next content change makes PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raise NoMethodError, crashing the hourly PollFeed run and skipping all remaining feed items, while topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the deleted topic's id so the embed iframe renders a dead topic forever.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally instantiates `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changes. Since `topic_embeds` has no FK/cascade in the migration and `TopicEmbed` has no `dependent: :destroy` on its associations, deleting the referenced post/topic can leave a `topic_embeds` row whose `post` association resolves to `nil`. That would make `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / subsequent calls raise, breaking the PollFeed loop/job. Also `topic_id_for_embed` will keep returning the stale `topic_id` as long as the orphaned row exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PollFeed spec only asserts the three gating settings and that execute delegates to poll_feed; the parsing/import loop itself (link fallback to i.id, CGI.unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import per item) has zero test coverage. The per-item crash behavior and URL/title handling ship completely untested — which is exactly where the NoMethodError defects in poll_feed live — so any regression in the actual import logic passes CI silently.

adjudication.rationale: The new job `Jobs::PollFeed` contains nontrivial per-item import logic in `poll_feed` (e.g., `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, `url = i.link` fallback to `i.id`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`). The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the gating conditions in `execute` and that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed`; it provides no coverage of the parsing/import loop or item field handling inside `poll_feed`, so regressions in that new logic would not be caught by CI. The claim about specific existing NoMethodError defects is not verifiable from the diff, but the missing coverage itself is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retrieved_recently? uses SETNX followed by a separate EXPIRE, so a worker killed between the two calls leaves the throttle key in Redis with no TTL. After such a crash (e.g., a deploy restarting Sidekiq mid-job), that embed URL is permanently throttled — TopicRetriever never fetches it again and visitors see 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely until someone manually deletes the key from Redis.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies between these two calls, the key can be left without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (throttled) forever for that embed_url, preventing `perform_retrieve` and leaving the embed stuck on the loading view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs as site-relative because they start with '/', rewriting src='//cdn.example.com/x' to 'http://blog.example.com//cdn.example.com/x'. Images and links from feeds or articles that use scheme-relative URLs (common for CDN-hosted assets) render broken inside imported posts, with no error surfaced to the admin configuring the feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` is treated as site-relative and rewritten to `"#{prefix}/#{...}"` after stripping leading slashes (`href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`). This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x`, incorrectly rewriting them to a URL under the origin host (e.g. `http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/x`) instead of preserving `//cdn.example.com/x` (or making it `http(s)://cdn...`). This breaks common CDN scheme-relative assets in imported content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds with no terminal failure state, and each reload of /embed/best re-enqueues a retrieve_topic job (throttled only to once per 60 seconds per URL). When retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username blank or misconfigured, article unfetchable), every visitor's iframe loops on 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely while the job queue absorbs a retrieve job per embedded URL per minute, and nothing surfaces the misconfiguration to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` every time `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, then renders `embed/loading`. `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(document.location.reload(), 30000)`), so users can get stuck in an infinite reload loop when a topic is never created. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the *work* to once/60s per URL via Redis, it does not prevent the controller from continually enqueuing jobs, so the queue can still be spammed (extra no-op jobs) during persistent failure/misconfiguration (e.g., retrieval can’t succeed). There is no terminal failure state or admin-facing feedback in this flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] RSS item content is passed through CGI.unescapeHTML and imported with zero HTML sanitization as a post with cook_method raw_html, so feed-supplied markup including <script> tags and inline event handlers is stored verbatim and rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:17 (and on normal topic pages, since Post#cook returns raw unmodified for raw_html). Anyone who can influence the polled feed's content (reader comments embedded in the feed, a compromised or third-party feed the admin points at) gets stored XSS on the forum origin: script executes for every viewer of the embedded comments or the imported topic, enabling session/cookie theft of admins; no sanitizer runs anywhere on this path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in app/models/post.rb). Feed polling imports `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). No sanitization/HTML filtering is applied anywhere on this path; `scrub` only addresses encoding. The embed view renders the result with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and because cooked==raw for `raw_html`, any feed-supplied `<script>` or event-handler attributes would be stored and rendered as HTML, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The source URL is interpolated unescaped into the imported post's HTML footer (`#{url}`), so a URL containing a single quote — which Ruby's URI parser accepts in query strings, e.g. `http://host/?y='onmouseover='alert(1)` — breaks out of the single-quoted href attribute, and feed-supplied links (PollFeed passes i.link through with only a ^http prefix regex) can inject arbitrary tags including

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the feed/article URL is interpolated directly into an HTML string using single-quoted attributes (`"#{url}"`) and then stored as post `raw` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which makes `Post#cook` return the raw HTML un-sanitized (`return raw if cook_method == ...`). The only validation on `url` is a `^https?://` regex, so a URL containing a single quote (e.g. in the query string) can break out of the `href` attribute and inject additional attributes/tags, leading to stored XSS when rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `embed/best.html.erb` (and in the topic itself). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs and does not sanitize, so it does not mitigate this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The SSRF guard compares only the initial URL's host string against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but the actual fetch in TopicEmbed.import_remote (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48) uses open(), which follows cross-host http->http redirects, and a string host comparison is defeated by DNS rebinding, so the fetch is not actually confined to the embeddable host. A malicious or compromised embedding site — the exact third party this feature admits — returns a 302 to an internal address (cloud metadata, internal services); open-uri follows it and the response body is imported as a public post, giving internal-network SSRF with read/exfiltration through the public topic, triggerable by any anonymous visitor with a spoofed Referer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces fetching remote content via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no redirect/target-host enforcement. The only host check in the new flow is `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, which compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb) before calling `import_remote`. Since `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default and DNS for the allowed hostname can change between check and fetch, the actual request can be made to a different host (including internal IPs), turning this into an SSRF read that is then stored as a public post via `TopicEmbed.import`/`PostCreator` (skip_validations, raw_html). This is a real security defect grounded in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The controller enqueues a retrieve_topic Sidekiq job for any user-supplied embed_url before any host validation or throttling runs (validation happens later inside the job via TopicRetriever), and TopicRetriever's throttle key is the full embed_url string, so varying the query string bypasses it entirely. Unauthenticated attackers (the Referer gate is satisfied by a spoofed header) flood the Sidekiq queue with arbitrary-length job payloads, create unbounded Redis keys via the per-URL setnx throttle, and trigger unbounded outbound fetches — a cheap queue/Redis exhaustion and fetch-amplification DoS against the forum.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` based solely on `params.require(:embed_url)`; the only pre-filter (`ensure_embeddable`) validates the *Referer* host, not the supplied `embed_url`. The actual `embed_url` host validation and throttling occur later in `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. The throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (full URL string), so attackers can bypass throttling by varying query strings/fragments and force many distinct Redis keys plus repeated fetches via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(... open(url) ...)`. Because referer is header-controlled and `current_user` can be nil, this enables unauthenticated queue/Redis growth and outbound fetch amplification (at least to the configured `embeddable_host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) routes through Kernel#open, which only delegates strings matching the scheme pattern to OpenURI and falls back to the original Kernel#open for everything else, so a settings value beginning with `|` is executed as a shell command. A feed_polling_url of `|<command>` (config-backed sink; treat the settings store as attacker-influenceable input) executes arbitrary commands on the app server during the hourly poll — remote code execution, not merely SSRF.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the new code does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. With OpenURI loaded, `Kernel#open` only delegates to OpenURI for strings that look like a URI scheme; otherwise it falls back to the original `Kernel#open`, which treats strings beginning with `|` as shell commands. Since `feed_polling_url` is taken directly from `SiteSetting` with no validation, a value like `|<command>` would execute on the server when the scheduled job runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddability gate authenticates the client using the Referer header, which is fully client-controlled and trivially spoofed by any non-browser client. Every protection downstream of this check (triggering server-side fetches, enqueueing jobs, rendering the embed view) is available to any anonymous internet attacker with curl -H 'Referer: ...'; the control only stops naive browser embedding, so it must not be relied on as a security boundary for the retrieval pipeline it guards.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated solely by `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and then `X-Frame-Options` is relaxed). Because `Referer` is a client-supplied header, a non-browser client can trivially spoof it and reach `best`, which (when no existing embed is found) enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` for an arbitrary `embed_url` param. That job ultimately can trigger server-side fetching via `TopicRetriever` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`open(url).read`) and/or feed polling (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), so the referer-based gate is acting as a security boundary for a retrieval pipeline even though it is not trustworthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ruby-readability allowlist preserves href values without any scheme validation, so javascript: URLs present in the source article survive extraction and are rendered raw in the embed page and topic. A reader clicking such a link in the embedded comments or the imported topic executes script in the forum origin — stored XSS via the same import path that the tag/attribute allowlist only partially mitigates; bites every viewer of imported articles from any source the admin imports from.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an import path that stores and renders raw HTML without sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `ruby-readability` with `tags: ... a ...` and `attributes: %w[href src]` and then passes `doc.content` into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`. Since neither `ruby-readability` nor `absolutize_urls` validates URL schemes, an `a href="javascript:..."` (or similar) in source content would survive extraction/import and be served to viewers, enabling stored XSS-on-click in the forum/embed origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of origin equality, so any sender whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted. A page at an origin contained within discourseUrl (e.g. intranet host https://forum when discourseUrl is https://forum.example.com/) passes the check and can forge resize messages; impact is limited to iframe height manipulation on the embedding page, but the origin control is defective as written.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag the same core flaw: using `indexOf`/substring containment for `postMessage` origin validation instead of strict origin equality, which allows attackers to bypass the check with crafted domains (golden: evil-discourseUrl.com; candidate: any origin that is a substring/contained).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never reaches params.require(:embed_url): the ensure_embeddable before_filter raises Discourse::InvalidAccess first (default-blank embeddable_host, and nil referer would also fail), so the test passes regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists. The missing-embed_url validation path (embed_controller.rb line 10) has zero coverage; replacing params.require(:embed_url) with params[:embed_url] lets nil flow into TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and Jobs.enqueue in production while this test and every other test in the diff stays green.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `ensure_embeddable` runs as a `before_filter` and raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` or if `request.referer` host mismatches (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). In the spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; ... end`, nothing stubs `embeddable_host` or `referer`, so the request is rejected by `ensure_embeddable` before the action reaches `params.require(:embed_url)`. Thus the test does not actually exercise/cover the missing-`embed_url` path, making it possible to regress `params.require` to `params[:embed_url]` without this spec failing. This is a test/coverage issue rather than a production bug in the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests never stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, so execute short-circuits on the default-false feed_polling_enabled? and poll_feed is skipped before the clauses these tests claim to verify are ever evaluated. Both tests pass even if the feed_polling_url.present? or embed_by_username.present? clauses are deleted from Jobs::PollFeed#execute, giving false confidence that each setting independently gates the hourly job.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples only stub feed_polling_url/embed_by_username to nil. Jobs::PollFeed#execute gates poll_feed behind `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. Since the site setting default for feed_polling_enabled is false (config/site_settings.yml), these tests will typically short-circuit on `feed_polling_enabled?` and never meaningfully test the other two clauses, so they can pass even if those conditions are removed. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only positive test verifies delegation by mocking poll_feed, so the entire poll_feed body — SimpleRSS parsing, the i.link/i.id URL fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and the TopicEmbed.import call — is never executed by any test (checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the only spec in the diff referencing PollFeed; every test interacts with poll_feed solely via mocha expectations). A regression in feed handling (e.g., i.content raising NoMethodError on feeds without a content element, or the URL fallback picking i.id) ships undetected; with sidekiq_options retry: false the hourly job then dies and imports silently stop in production.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the only “positive” test stubs settings and asserts `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`, which replaces/avoids executing the real `poll_feed` implementation. No other added spec calls `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` without mocking, so the new feed-handling logic (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, `i.link`/`i.id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`) is not exercised by tests in this diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both positive-path tests stub retrieved_recently? and mock perform_retrieve, so the real throttle logic ($redis.setnx with 60-second expire), the TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists? dedupe, the feed-polling branch, and fetch_http's embed_by_username lookup are never executed (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb — the only spec referencing TopicRetriever; all five tests stub or mock these methods). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic inside TopicRetriever#retrieve / #retrieved_recently? / #perform_retrieve (Redis throttle via $redis.setnx + expire, dedupe via TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?, feed polling branch, and fetch_http user lookup by SiteSetting.embed_by_username). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update test only exercises the changed-content path: the unchanged-content dedup branch (content_sha1 equality short-circuit) is never executed and the persisted update of embed.content_sha1 via update_column is never asserted. A regression that drops embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) or breaks the sha1 comparison passes the suite while every hourly PollFeed run re-revises the same post, spamming post revisions indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the dedup/short-circuit behavior depends on `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and the changed-content path persists the new sha via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. The spec `"Supports updating the post"` only exercises the changed-content branch by supplying different contents, and it never asserts that `topic_embeds.content_sha1` was updated (nor does any test exercise the unchanged-content branch where the method should *not* revise). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_embed_spec.rb covers only .import; TopicEmbed.import_remote — the Readability extraction with its tag/attribute whitelist and the opts[:title] || doc.title fallback that both TopicRetriever.fetch_http and the rewritten disqus:import task now depend on — is never called by any test, and .topic_id_for_embed is only ever mocked (embed_controller_spec.rb lines 41/49), never run against real data. adjudication.rationale: Diff adds nontrivial new behavior in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `ruby-readability`, whitelist `tags`/`attributes`, and `opts[:title] || doc.title` fallback) and makes it a dependency of `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`) and the rewritten `disqus:import` task (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The success-context specs stub TopicView and rspec-rails controller specs do not render views unless render_views is called, so embed/best.html.erb, embed/loading.html.erb and layouts/embed.html.erb are never compiled or executed by any test in the diff — including the unusual '<%- end if %>' terminator in best.html.erb and the resize postMessage script in the layout. A template syntax or runtime error (in the posts loop, the avatar/cooked rendering, or the layout's postMessage call) would 500 every embed request in production while the suite stays green; the loading-vs-best template choice is also unverifiable since response bodies are empty.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the tests call `get :best` and assert status/headers, but never enable `render_views`, and they stub out key objects (`TopicView.expects(:new)` / `TopicRetriever`). In rspec-rails controller specs, views are not rendered/compiled unless `render_views` is used, so the newly added templates (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) and layout (`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`) are not exercised by any spec in the diff.
