This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 backfills every existing post with the value 1, but Post.cook_methods = Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns sequential values starting at 0, so the default 1 maps to :raw_html instead of :regular. Every pre-existing post is reclassified as raw_html and every newly created regular post inherits the same column default (PostCreator only assigns cook_method when the option is passed, so all normal posts get the default), so Post#cook returns raw markdown site-wide: any edit or recook persists uncooked markdown into the cooked column and the rendering pipeline (markdown, emoji, oneboxes) silently disappears for all content.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on an assumption not shown in the diff: that `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` assigns values starting at 0. The diff provides no definition of `Enum`, and the migration explicitly sets `cook_method` default to `1`, which is consistent with an Enum implementation that starts at 1 (common in this codebase, e.g. `Post.types = Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` elsewhere). If the Enum starts at 1, then default `1` correctly maps to `:regular` and does not reclassify all posts as `:raw_html`. Therefore the alleged site-wide breakage cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] force: true is added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, turning its create_table into drop-and-recreate of the existing top_topics table on any re-run. Re-executing the migration (db:migrate:redo, a restored or hand-patched schema_migrations, or a retry after a partial failure) silently drops top_topics and all its computed per-period ranking rows instead of failing loudly on the existing table; a workaround for a dirty dev database has been shipped inside a migration that production databases have already applied.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. Because this is an already-existing (not newly added) migration file, any re-run/redo of that migration (e.g., `db:migrate:redo` or in cases where the migration is replayed) would silently drop `top_topics` and its data instead of failing, creating a data-loss risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topic_embeds is created with topic_id/post_id reference columns but no foreign keys and no cleanup path anywhere in the diff, so destroying an imported topic leaves the topic_embeds row dangling permanently. After a user deletes an imported topic, TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the dead topic id so embed/best renders an error in the external site's iframe forever, and TopicRetriever permanently refuses to re-import because perform_retrieve bails when TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...).exists? is true; when the feed content later changes, import takes the update path with embed.post nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError, killing the retry:false PollFeed run and skipping every remaining feed item.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` columns but adds only a unique index on `embed_url` (no FK constraints) and the `TopicEmbed` model has plain `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no `dependent:` cleanup shown. Several new code paths assume the referenced records exist: `EmbedController#best` treats any `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` as valid and builds `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` permanently bails out on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` without checking that the topic/post still exist. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` if content changed; if the post was deleted but the `topic_embeds` row remains, `embed.post` can be `nil`, causing an exception. This is a real correctness issue unless there is external cleanup not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] create_table :topic_embeds, force: true makes this new migration destructive on re-run instead of failing loudly when the table already exists. An operator running db:migrate:redo for this version after the embedding feature has accumulated data silently drops every embed_url-to-topic mapping; the next feed poll or embed view then imports the same article as a duplicate topic, splitting the discussion in two.

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. Re-running this migration (e.g., via `db:migrate:redo` for that version) would therefore silently delete all existing `topic_embeds` rows, losing the `embed_url`→`topic_id`/`post_id` mapping. Subsequent code (e.g., `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` in `EmbedController#best` / `TopicRetriever`) would no longer find the mapping and could re-import the same URL, creating a new topic and effectively duplicating/splitting discussions as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed_url is typed as t.string (varchar(255)) while the code inserts arbitrary article and feed-link URLs, so any URL longer than 255 characters raises a 'value too long' error on insert. TopicEmbed.import raises inside its transaction (rolling back the post creation as well), and because PollFeed sets sidekiq_options retry: false, a single over-long link in the feed kills the entire polling run and every feed item after it is never imported on that run or any subsequent hourly run while the item stays in the feed.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `t.string :embed_url` with no explicit limit, which in Rails maps to `varchar(255)` by default. The code stores external URLs from RSS/Atom (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.link`/`i.id`) and from HTTP retrieval (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, url, ...)`) into `topic_embeds.embed_url` via `TopicEmbed.create!`. There is no length validation or truncation, and `create!` is inside a `Topic.transaction`, so an over-255 URL would raise and roll back post creation. `Jobs::PollFeed` has no rescue and sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single too-long URL can abort the polling run, and since the hourly job will encounter the same feed item again, it can repeatedly prevent importing items after it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The header block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` with no condition expression after the `if` keyword, so the template fails ERB/Erubis compilation with a SyntaxError. Every request that renders this view — any embed_url that already has a topic — raises ActionView::Template::Error and returns a 500 instead of the comments page, so the feature only works while it shows 'Loading...' and breaks exactly once the topic exists; the controller specs pass because they never render views.
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue point to the same underlying bug: the ERB template closes an if-block with `<%- end if %>`, which produces invalid Ruby (`end if` without a condition) and causes a render-time SyntaxError. The fix is to use just `end` to close the block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When no topic exists the controller fire-and-forgets Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) and renders a loading page whose only mechanism is an unconditional 30-second reload loop with no terminal state. If retrieval fails for any reason (remote URL unreachable, readability/import error, embed_by_username unset, host mismatch), no error is ever surfaced: the iframe shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely, and every 30-second reload enqueues another RetrieveTopic job, so a permanently broken URL produces an endless reload/job loop per open embed page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an embed flow where `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, then renders `embed/loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), and there is no terminal/error state. If retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is blank, or remote fetch/import fails), the iframe will stay on “Loading…” and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job, creating an endless reload/job loop per open embed page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'retrieved recently' redis marker is committed (setnx + expire) before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed retrieval leaves the marker in place for its full 60-second TTL. Every retry within the next 60 seconds — retries of the failed job and the loading page's 30-second re-enqueues — enters retrieve, sees the marker, and returns success without attempting the work, so the system reports success while the retrieval never happened; recovery depends entirely on the user keeping the page open past the throttle window.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle marker is set via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` *before* `perform_retrieve` is called (`retrieve` does `perform_retrieve unless ... retrieved_recently?`). If `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote` fails (network/readability/open errors, etc.) or returns without creating the embed, the redis key still remains for 60s, causing subsequent calls within that window to return early and skip retrieval. This interacts with `EmbedController#best` rendering `loading` (reloads every 30s) and enqueuing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so repeated attempts can be suppressed by the throttle despite no embed being created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] setnx and expire are two separate redis calls, so a crash or redis error between them leaves the throttle key set with no TTL. The orphaned key makes retrieved_recently? return true forever for that embed_url, permanently and silently blocking retrieval for it (loading page forever) until someone manually deletes the key or Redis is flushed.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses two separate Redis calls: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or Redis errors after `setnx` but before `expire`, the key can be left without a TTL. On subsequent calls `setnx` will fail, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return `true` indefinitely for that `@embed_url`, preventing `perform_retrieve` from running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline and lets its exceptions propagate, so embed retrieval is coupled to feed health and aborts before fetch_http is reached. With feed_polling_enabled and a broken feed (unreachable URL, non-feed response, or the per-item crash in the loop), every embed retrieval for every URL fails as a job error instead of falling through to the HTTP path; even a healthy feed forces each retrieval to run the entire feed import synchronously inside the job.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` the code runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before `fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` with no error handling (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so network errors, parse errors, or item-level exceptions will propagate and abort `perform_retrieve` before `fetch_http` is reached. This couples embed retrieval success to feed health and also forces a full feed poll synchronously on every embed retrieval attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote buffers the entire response of open(url).read into memory with no size cap and passes no open/read timeout options. The fetch is reachable from the public embed flow for any URL whose host matches embeddable_host, so a large response exhausts the Sidekiq worker's memory, and a server that drips bytes slower than the per-read timeout keeps the worker hung indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (lib/topic_embed.rb) with no size cap and no timeout options. This is invoked from the public embed flow: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` for any `embed_url` whose host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). Reading the entire response into memory can exhaust a Sidekiq worker on a large response, and without explicit timeouts/limits a slow-drip response can tie up the worker for an unbounded duration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The throttle key is the full embed_url string ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}"), so it imposes no limit across URLs, and EmbedController#best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job on every cache-miss request with no other rate limit. A client (the referer check is a client-supplied header) that varies the path on embeddable_host bypasses the throttle entirely, driving unbounded server-side fetch+import jobs and unbounded topic creation from a public endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a public GET /embed/best endpoint (routes.rb) that, on cache miss (no TopicEmbed for params[:embed_url]), unconditionally enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic (EmbedController#best) with no rate limiting at enqueue time. RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever does have throttling, but it keys on the full URL string (`retrieved_key = "retrieved:#{@embed_url}"` in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?), so varying the path/query on the allowed host bypasses the 60s throttle entirely while still passing the host check (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). Since `ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` (client-supplied header) for authorization, a non-browser client can spoof it and drive repeated server-side `open(url)` fetches and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicEmbed.import` topic creation for many distinct URLs on the embeddable host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_http returns silently when the embed_by_username setting does not resolve to an existing user (blank setting, typo, renamed account). Retrieval no-ops with no log line and no error result, so every embed on the site shows the loading page forever with nothing in the logs to explain why.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, the code resolves the posting user via `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then does `return if user.blank?` (silent no-op). When `EmbedController#best` can’t find an existing `TopicEmbed`, it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading`; if the configured `embed_by_username` doesn’t map to a real user, the job will never create the embed/topic and the iframe stays on the loading page (which reloads every 30s) with no logged error or response indicating misconfiguration. This behavior is directly shown by the diff and matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dedup key is the embed_url string compared verbatim (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) and topic_id_for_embed) with no URL normalization anywhere in the import/lookup path. The same article reached via textually different URLs (trailing slash, http vs https, feed link vs the blog's canonical permalink) creates duplicate topics, and the embed iframe on one variant never finds the other variant's topic and re-triggers retrieval.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces embed/topic import keyed solely by the literal URL string: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` in `topic_id_for_embed`, with no normalization/canonicalization step anywhere in the new code path. `EmbedController#best` looks up by the raw `params[:embed_url]` and will enqueue retrieval when that exact string isn't found. As a result, textually different URLs for the same article (e.g., http vs https, trailing slash, different but equivalent permalinks) will create distinct `topic_embeds` rows (unique index enforces uniqueness only per string), leading to duplicate topics and missed lookups/retrieval re-triggers for alternate variants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed_url is a varchar(255) with a unique index, and import inserts the URL verbatim with no length handling. Any article URL longer than 255 characters (common with tracking parameters) makes TopicEmbed.create! raise inside import's transaction, repeatedly failing the RetrieveTopic job and leaving that embed permanently on the loading page.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `t.string :embed_url, null: false` with no limit, which in Rails maps to a 255-length varchar by default, and adds a unique index on it. `TopicEmbed.import` then uses the provided `url` verbatim in `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` with no length validation/truncation/normalization. If an `embed_url` exceeds the column length, the create! will raise inside the transaction, and the embed won’t be created; `EmbedController#best` renders the loading page whenever `topic_id_for_embed` is nil and only enqueues retrieval, so an unrecoverable create failure can leave the embed perpetually “loading”.
